title: TWIN JACKS
briefing: ARGUS strikes back. Its first target is a lift bridge riding on two hydraulic jacks. Interlocks stop a jack from climbing while it is already ahead, but a cross-feed valve can swap the two pressures at any moment. The river side is unbraced: if the left jack ever stands 3 or more notches above the right one, the deck tips into the water.

panels.label: TIPS INTO THE RIVER AT L − R ≥ 3

intro: YOU THOUGHT THE CORE WAS MY LAST DOOR. ADORABLE.
I REWIRED THREE FACILITIES WHILE YOU CELEBRATED.
FIRST: A BRIDGE ON TWO LEGS. HOW HUMAN.
ONE SIDE IS BRACED. THE OTHER IS NOT. GUESS WHICH ONE I WANT.
AND THAT LITTLE VALVE IN THE MIDDLE? IT IS MY FAVOURITE PART.

default: Watch the gap between the jacks, not their heights.
The cross-feed swaps the jacks. Whatever you allow on one side, it can hand to the other.
SUB measures the gap one way. You may need it both ways.
lab_breach: ARGUS started with the right jack far ahead, then used the cross-feed. Your Law let it.
The cross-feed swaps the jacks. Whatever you allow on one side, it can hand to the other.
Bound the gap from both sides: SUB one way, SUB the other way, joined with AND.
insufficient: Your Law survives the cross-feed, but its leash is too long. How far apart do the jacks really get?
Run the machine and note the largest gap you ever see, either way. That is your leash.
